_comment: Shared by the Godot game (game/) and the Python backend (backend/). Units: robot mm, world cm.

robot._z_note: Z is reported by the backend in abstract 'z units' (0..z_max) derived from the STS3020 ID1 drum servo count (SERVO_STATUS abs=). The firmware has no Z homing; the backend defines 0 at the position seen when 'z_zero' is sent. If a LARGER value means the arm is HIGHER set z_up_is_positive=true. The on-screen rope is longest when the arm is highest (inverse mapping).

world._fit_note: true: the robot's X range spans the play area width (computed at runtime from the window, the debug panel and the projection); false: fixed travel_x_cm.

audio._note: Sound effects from 効果音ラボ (soundeffect-lab.info). In game/assets/audio/ as part of the game; do not hand the files out on their own (see SOURCES.md there). up/down = the UFO rising/sinking on screen (arm going down/up).

pose_direction._note: Hand shape per direction (robot axes [x, y, z]; +X right, +Y away, +Z arm up). open = パー, peace = チョキ, fist = グー, point = 指差し (only the index out), thumb_up / thumb_down = いいね (index..pinky folded, thumb out) with the thumb towards the top / bottom of the camera view as shown (view flip_v and joystick invert_z apply; within thumb_min_vertical of vertical, else no sign). Default: point = where the finger points, thumbs-up up / down = arm up / down, claw: open (パー) = open, peace (チョキ) = closed, held claw_hold_ms; fist (グー) = nothing (rest the hand). "finger" = where the index finger points (any angle, or snapped to point_snap_deg; image -> robot axes with the joystick invert_x / invert_y / swap_xy; shorter than point_min_len hand sizes = pointing at the camera = no motion). A shape counts after pose_confirm_ms; a confirmed one survives a flicker shorter than pose_release_ms; another shape stops first, then arms again. After a forced stop the shape must be gone for pose_release_ms. A shape used for a direction never moves the claw. Untested with the real camera / robot.

gesture._note: Pinch hand joystick (backend: --gesture). scheme = how the game reads the hand (pinch_joystick = this pinch stick, pose_direction = a hand shape per direction; settings of other schemes go in schemes.<id>; switching always stops the gesture). delegate = gpu (Metal: faster, and frees the CPU for the game). MediaPipe 1.1.1's GPU path keeps one image per frame (~1 GB per 30 s, aborting after ~8 min with 'Error creating pixel buffer: -6662') until the landmarker is closed, so it is rebuilt on a thread and swapped in every gpu_recreate_s. detection_confidence / tracking_confidence = MediaPipe's thresholds (tracking low so a fast, blurred hand is kept). pinch_start 1.0 / pinch_release 1.5 / confirm 0 were tuned by hand on the C270 (open the hand wide to release: check the ratio goes above 1.5). stale_ms = an event older than this stops the stick (CPU MediaPipe frames occasionally take 200-280 ms on an M4 MacBook Air; 150 stopped every few seconds). camera = part of the gesture camera's name (or an index). Pinch = |thumb tip - index tip| / hand size (the larger of |index MCP - pinky MCP| and 0.75 x |wrist - middle MCP|): starts <= pinch_start held pinch_confirm_ms, ends >= pinch_release held release_confirm_ms (tunable live from the debug panel: the gesture_config command). A hand lost (or a second hand / ambiguous) for less than lost_grace_ms keeps the last good frame (MediaPipe drops a moving hand for a frame or two). min_confidence gates the left/right score (0 = off: it drops for a hand seen from above). roi = operating region [x0, y0, x1, y1] in normalised image coords (keep it outside the crane's reach). joystick: radius = fraction of the image short side, deadzone / full = fractions of the radius, speed = ((r - deadzone)/(full - deadzone))^curve * max_speed_mm_s. allow_real_robot: true since the gesture was checked with the mock (2026-10-25); the robot must still be connected, motors on, homed, no alarm, nothing else moving (H toggles the mode).

camera._note: USB cameras by role (C270 = overview / gesture, Innomaker U20CAM = arm tip): overview = looks down on the desk (gesture detection later), focus = on the arm tip. match = part of the camera name (empty = none; pick one in the debug panel). The scope view shows focus, or overview when there is no focus camera. Frames are only drawn: never saved or sent.

study.system_prompt: あなたは画像を見ながら学習を支援する家庭教師です。答えだけでなく、考え方を段階的に日本語で説明してください。画像にない事実は推測と明記してください。
study._note: Optional and off by default. It runs only when enabled here and the backend is started with --study. provider: claude (Claude Code CLI, signed in; claude is looked for in ~/.local/bin, Homebrew and the newest VS Code / Cursor extension when not on PATH; ~ is allowed) or codex (codex app-server). No tools, no MCP, no settings; no credentials are stored here.

approach._note: 近づいてアドバイス (#76): Z to the top, XY to the spot recorded with homework_spot_set (config/homework_spot.json) or to a clicked overview point (#78), claws open (open_claw: the arm hangs from the rope and its camera cable can tilt it; standing on its open claws the camera looks straight down, so record the spot where the open claws stand on the worksheet), Z down to its height, wait for the game's capture (at most hold_timeout_s), Z back to the top (claws closed if close_claw_after), XY back to where it started (return_xy). Holds the motion lock like the auto catch; stop / soft_stop / motors off / the operator leaving / any fault end it with the robot's stop (ABORT). Not yet run on the real robot.

camera_map._note: Overview camera image -> CoreXY XY (#78): a homography fitted to points recorded in the 宿題 tab (arm camera centred on a mark, the mark clicked in the overview image), saved in config/camera_xy_calibration.json. Not used to move when the fit's largest error is over max_error_mm, when the camera's size / flips changed since calibration, or for a point more than margin_mm outside the calibrated points. Not yet run on the real robot.

homework._note: Homework watch (F1 panel tab). While started, the overview camera is captured every interval_s and the worksheet's progress is estimated with Cloudflare Workers AI typesafe/jev-1.14.0 (method verified in ~/python_ws/jev: 3 questions per call, about 8.8k tokens / $0.00037 per call). The key is CF_ACCOUNT_ID / CF_API_TOKEN from the environment or the repository's .env (never committed; see .env.example). Frames go to Cloudflare and are not stored here. Stall: the shown progress has not grown by stall_min_gain points for stall_s (not at 100%, not while a hand covers the sheet); the panel then offers an advice by the study assistant (study.provider: Claude Code / Codex, no --study needed), and again only after another stall_s.

backend._note: z_counts_per_unit: servo counts per abstract Z unit (4096 counts/turn; 3 turns = 12288 counts = 100 units). z_sign: +1 if positive SERVO_TURN raises the arm, -1 otherwise (set on the real machine). jog_max_mm_s: speed cap for serial JOG (firmware recommends <= 50 mm/s).

auto_catch._note: One-button auto catch (backend/src/corexy_ufo_backend/sequence/). Z in the backend's z units (robot.z_min..z_max; z_max = arm at the top, the z_zero reference), XY in mm, times in s. 'real' drives the real crane: every null must be measured on the machine and every 'confirmed' item set true by hand after checking it there, otherwise the backend refuses auto_catch on the real robot. 'dry_run' is used only with --mock / --auto-catch-dry-run: made-up values for the virtual crane, never for the real robot. Accelerations and the servo speed are fixed in the firmware (XY 1000 mm/s^2, servo 2400 counts/s): they only drive the dry-run model. Polarity: the home limit switches are read by the firmware (active LOW, 30 ms debounce) and reach the host as LIMIT_X/LIMIT_Y=ACTIVE|OPEN; there is no physical E-stop input (stop = ABORT command); the catch button is the game's C key (no electrical polarity).
